newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African rand/dollar futures seen slow at start.
newsitem.headline: S.African rand/dollar futures seen slow at start.

text.p: Volumes traded in rand/dollar futures contracts were likely to be sluggish to start with, but would pick up when exchange controls were eased further, foreign exchange traders siad on Tuesday.

The South African Futures Exchange's (Safex) announced earlier that it would begin trading rand/dollar futures on April 30, but that trade in the contracts would be limited to non-resident clients of Safex members and authorised dealers.
"Initially it will be slowish until more restrictions are eased and then it will probably take off," Standard Bank's director of foreign exchange Willie Potgieter said.
"But we would welcome the introduction of the future as banks because it is certainly another instrument that we can use."

Another senior trader who did not want to be named said: "The fact that they are setting it up is a good sign because it helps to keep the market in sync in terms of arbitrage opportunities and efficiency."

"In the short-term, however, it is limited to authorised dealers, which is quite limiting in terms of volumes. But as time goes on and more pepople are allowed to speculate and/or hedge, it should pick up," he said.

Because volumes were expected to initially be low, traders said that in the short-term, while the contracts would provide an alternative to the forward market, they were unlikely to have any impact on forward market volumes.
"The dollar/rand forward market does massive volumes and I don't think to start off the future will be able to handle those volumes," the trader said.
The underlying instrument on the futures will be the spot rand/dollar exchange rate, quoted to four decimal places, and contracts will be valued at $100,000 each.

Expiry dates would follow the same cycle as equity contracts -- March, June, September and December -- with expiry prices determined by taking a notional offer to buy and sell from six authorised dealers at the expiry time, followed by the arithmetic average of the middle four rates.
The futures will be cash settled in rand.
Safex will list options on futures with strike prices at intervals of 0.01 rand/dollar.
